notes: Fifth-role independent agent review of all 15 merged records: discovery (10), diamond expansion (5), and every fee/ranking patch were read. Full-field patches replace route, formats, review, difficulty, metrics and scope_notes without editing the four original role files or canonical directory. Policy pages, not search snippets, supply the substantive new evidence.

Independent current official-page checks covered each journal's fees and author guidance, ordinary peer review, article types, stated length/format constraints, optional versus compulsory costs, and material preprint/AI workflow restrictions. No general word/page cap was identified for ordinary Psychological Research, Memory & Cognition, JDM, Meta-Psychology or QCMB in the inspected guidance; that is a bounded negative finding, not permission for unlimited length. No compulsory membership/registration or mandatory paid editing service was identified. Current fee-policy availability is not a logged-in portal test.

Fee outcome remains 12 verified_free and three needs_verification. Seven Sage journal-specific statements exclude submission/publication fees. Meta-Psychology's blanket completely-free/no-processing-fees statement reasonably covers submission; that interpretation remains explicit. Methodology and QCMB also have direct journal-specific submission/publication-fee exclusions (https://meth.psychopen.eu/index.php/meth/policies ; https://qcmb.psychopen.eu/index.php/qcmb/policies), supplementing the applicable PsychOpen entire-process policy. Springer's no-APC subscription routes leave other mandatory-cost evidence incomplete. JDM is currently paid Gold OA with conditional full waivers/coverage, not diamond.

Independent numerical checks reproduced Sage PSPB 18.4%, GPIR 13.4%, Theory & Psychology 10.0%, and EJP 17.4%. APM 13.0% remains the ranking agent's separately recorded official first-hand evidence; repeated reviewer browser retrievals timed out and ordinary urllib returned HTTP 403, so this review does not claim independent reproduction of that value. All five retain the official Sage definition: final accept/reject decisions across all article types during the previous calendar year, not an externally reviewed-only population or initial-submission cohort. The dashboards print neither year nor denominator counts. Any mapping to 2025 from a 2026 check is explicitly inferential. Definition independently read: https://www.sagepub.com/journals/understanding-journal-metrics .

Independently reproduced all eight explicitly 2025 citation values (Psychological Research 2.1/2.5 JIF/5-year JIF; Memory & Cognition 1.8/2.5; Methodology JIF 3.1/CiteScore 3.7; SPB JIF 2.3/CiteScore 2.7) and the JDM 2024 volume-based counts of 35 research-type articles and 35 Gold OA articles. Read publisher metric definitions, including https://www.elsevier.support/scopus/answer/what-is-citescore and https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/authors/journal-publishing-statistics. Citation impact and published article volume do not establish acceptance odds. No new stale or unyear-labelled citation number was entered.

Difficulty adjudication keeps five provisional high agent judgments supported by official decision-rate evidence plus specific contribution gates. FAP high and Meta-Psychology moderate become unknown: originality/scarcity and a no-quota/no-novelty model do not establish comparative difficulty. All remaining bands are unknown. No total ordering across specialties or discipline-wide acceptance probabilities is established.

All seven Sage author pages link the current publisher AI policy (https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/artificial-intelligence-policy). It distinguishes assistive editing from disclosed generative use and separately lists prohibited uses, including generating a submission through a series of prompts, experiences/themes analysis, fabricated evidence and confidentiality breaches. This directory review does not adjudicate a specific manuscript workflow. Theory & Psychology is stricter: explicit editor permission plus full disclosure. SPB prohibits original AI-written text even with disclosure and permits editing/translation only with disclosure. For Meta-Psychology, Methodology, QCMB and Psychological Thought, no general original-generative-AI permission was established from the inspected pages; an absent restriction or Grammarly reference is not affirmative permission.

Independently checked PsychOpen GOLD's notice of discontinuation by 31 December 2027 and continuing transition support (https://psychopen.eu/). Retained successor-publisher/fee/status uncertainty for Methodology, SPB and QCMB. Psychological Thought's current university publisher since January 2020 is independently established on its About/history page and is not assigned the current platform closure.

Independently rechecked all three excluded paused leads: JNC currently pauses submissions for a publisher move and separately says support ends September 2027 (https://jnc.psychopen.eu/); EJOP remains paused from 18 February 2026 until further notice (https://ejop.psychopen.eu/); JSPP remains paused from 4 May 2026 and announces a new Universidad de O'Higgins platform with reopening planned early 2027 (https://jspp.psychopen.eu/). None is represented as reopened; their recent accepted-article publication and generic New submission links do not override notices.

This is an independent agent review of directory evidence, not journal peer review, human scientific review, manuscript suitability, rights/ethics approval or a guarantee of acceptance/costs. No editor contact, login, submission, remote write or portal transaction occurred. The review adds no clinical-practice or new physical-laboratory opportunity to OSRI's initial scope.
